requirement: Split dataset rows into train and test index sets reproducibly from a seed, without disturbing any other code that relies on NumPy's global random state.
skeleton: train_test_indices validating n and the fraction, permuting with a seeded default_rng, clamping the test size to leave both sides non-empty, and returning sorted index arrays.
caption: A reproducible train and test split of sample indices using a local NumPy Generator. train_test_indices(n, test_fraction, *, seed) raises ValueError saying at least 2 samples are needed when n is below 2, and ValueError saying test_fraction must be strictly between 0 and 1 otherwise. It creates np.random.default_rng(seed), so the global np.random state is never touched, and permutes range n. The test size is round of n times the fraction, clamped to at least 1 and at most n minus 1 so both sides are non-empty. It returns the remaining and the first n_test permuted indices, each sorted. The fixture asserts that seed 7 repeats while seed 8 differs, that 10 samples at 0.3 form a sorted partition with 3 test rows, that 0.01 and 0.9 still leave one sample on each side, that the global random stream is unchanged, and that fractions 0 and 1 and n of 1 raise ValueError.

constraints: test_fraction must be strictly between 0 and 1
A local default_rng(seed) is used, not global state
Both train and test get at least one index
Returned index arrays are sorted and partition range n

rationale.teaches: Use a local Generator for reproducibility and clamp derived sizes so rounding never produces an empty split.
rationale.why: Seeding the global RNG changes other components' random streams, and rounding tiny fractions to zero yields an empty test set.

ops.docstring: Reproducible train/test index splits with a local NumPy Generator.

candidates.why_wrong: Seeding the global RNG changes random numbers drawn elsewhere in the program.
A tiny test fraction rounds to an empty test set.
A large test fraction can leave the training set empty.
Index arrays come back in shuffled order instead of sorted.
Fractions of exactly 0 or 1 are accepted instead of rejected.
